records.text: Pastor Hyun-bo Son was jailed in South Korea on election-law charges, raising concerns among supporters about religious freedom.
records.speaker: Lucille Talusan

appearances.snippet: His imprisonment has raised concerns about religious freedom in South Korea. ... Pastor Hyun-bo Son remains jailed in South Korea on election law charges and has drawn attention from the Korean administration for his stance on biblical truths.

verification.notes: Contemporary and subsequent reporting confirms Son was jailed on election-law charges and that supporters framed the case as a religious-freedom issue. He was later convicted and released after about five months; the episode’s present-tense wording was accurate when published.

sources.title: Support Grows for Imprisoned Korean Pastor After Son Speaks at AmFest — CBN News
sources.relevance: Reports Son’s detention on election-law charges and supporters’ religious-freedom concerns.

sources.title: South Korean Pastor Out of Prison After Election-Law Conviction — CBN News
sources.relevance: Later outcome confirms the prosecution, conviction, and release after roughly five months.

records.text: Hyun-bo Son was arrested two days after meeting Charlie Kirk, after warning Kirk that his arrest was possible.
records.speaker: Chance Son

appearances.snippet: the possibility that my father could get arrested. And in fact, my father got arrested two days after he met Charlie.

verification.notes: The cited report records Chance Son’s firsthand account that his father discussed the arrest risk with Charlie Kirk and was arrested two days after their meeting. The timing is independently consistent with the reported September 4 meeting and September 9 arrest, though the warning itself rests on Chance Son’s testimony.

sources.title: Support Grows for Imprisoned Korean Pastor After Son Speaks at AmFest — CBN News
sources.relevance: Contains Chance Son’s account of the meeting, warning, and arrest two days later.

records.text: Charlie Kirk promised Hyun-bo Son that he would use his platform to publicize Son’s situation in South Korea.
records.speaker: Chance Son

appearances.snippet: Charlie made sure that he will use his platform and his voice to let the whole world and America know that this is happening in South Korea.

verification.notes: The cited report contains Chance Son’s direct account that Kirk promised to use his platform and voice to publicize the situation. This supports attribution as Son’s firsthand testimony; no recording or independent witness account of the promise was located.

sources.title: Support Grows for Imprisoned Korean Pastor After Son Speaks at AmFest — CBN News
sources.relevance: Contains Chance Son’s account of Kirk’s promise to publicize the case.

records.text: Hyun-bo Son was accused of violating South Korea’s Public Official Election Act and Local Education Autonomy Act after political remarks at a Christian protest.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: he was accused of violating the Public Official Election Act and the Local Education Autonomy Act... The conservative pastor participated in a protest... he shouted the words that Lee Jae-myung has to die for Korea to live.

verification.notes: Reporting confirms that Son was accused under the Public Official Election Act and Local Education Autonomy Act over political statements associated with church activity and a protest. Later reporting says he was convicted; the sources used are advocacy-oriented, so confidence is medium rather than high.

sources.title: Targeted Arrest? South Korean Pastor Held on Election Charges — CBN News
sources.relevance: Contemporary account identifies the statutes and political remarks involved in Son’s arrest.

sources.title: South Korean Pastor Out of Prison After Election-Law Conviction — CBN News
sources.relevance: Later report confirms the charges resulted in a conviction and release.
